meanings.note: With things and places. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to like'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aimé').
With people. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to like'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aimé').

examples.text: Tu n'aimais pas Mandelieu? C'est un bel endroit.
examples.trans: Didn't you like Mandelieu? It's a lovely place.

meanings.note: Arrête! / arrêtez!. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to stop'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'arrêté').
Arrête! / arrêtez!. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to stop'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'arrêté').

examples.text: Il arrête de travailler à six heures.
Sans toi, je crois que j'arrêterais ce métier.
examples.trans: Without you, I think I'd quit this job.

meanings.note: Une autre = another (one). Descriptive French adjective meaning 'other'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Also a pronoun. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'other'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à quatorze heures. Je vais déjeuner deux fois.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two. I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé

meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

changer de + noun without article: changer d'agent
Comparison: comme un rêve. Core French preposition meaning 'like', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Conjunction. Core French preposition meaning 'like', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard masculine noun meaning 'opposite'.
Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard masculine noun meaning 'opposite'.

examples.text: Tu devrais le lui dire. Il a l'air de penser le contraire.

Dans une heure = in an hour. Core French preposition meaning 'in', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Tu connais beaucoup de monde dans le cinéma. Tu pourrais m'aider.

meanings.note: À demain = see you tomorrow. Invariable French adverb meaning 'tomorrow'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

meanings.note: Conjugated like 'ouvrir'. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Core French verb meaning 'to discover, to find out'.

examples.trans: Colette Brancillon is going to find out.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.
